gaps.description: The doc has Text and Bytes but no character or code point type, and no literal for one such as U+FFFD, so Rune is assumed.
No multiple results, tuple destructuring or discard; a helper record is declared and one field read.
The doc uses `Bytes` both as a type of data (example 20) and as a unit of size (`size as Bytes at most 1 GiB`, `offset as Bytes`), so it is unclear whether Bytes is a byte sequence or a quantity.

notes: Behaviour is exact provided decode_rune keeps Go's no-failure, replacement-character semantics. A Scribe library would likely make invalid UTF-8 a `fails with` or a maybe, which would be a different contract from Go's; the doc gives no guidance on sentinel-value conventions like RuneError. Example 27 uses Bytes as a size unit and example 20 as data, which is a naming collision worth resolving.
